title: Number of Wonderful Substrings
summary: A wonderful string allows at most one character to appear an odd number of times.
statement: A wonderful string allows at most one character to appear an odd number of times. Count all non-empty substrings of 'word' that meet this criterion, considering each occurrence separately.
constraints: word has 1 through 100000 letters from a through j.
A substring is wonderful when at most one character count is odd.
Count occurrences by position, including identical substring text at different positions.
hints: A ten-bit prefix mask records which character counts are currently odd.
A substring has zero odd counts when its endpoint masks match, or one odd count when the masks differ by one bit.
For each prefix, add frequencies of the same mask and all ten one-bit neighbors, then record the current mask.
XOR of two prefix parity masks is exactly the substring parity mask, so the counted cases are necessary and sufficient.
editorial: XOR of two prefix parity masks is exactly the substring parity mask, so the counted cases are necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: The wonderful substrings are a, b, a, and aba, for four total.
Nine of the ten substrings qualify; only the middle substring ab has two odd-frequency characters.
